questions.q: What does SYSTEM$CLASSIFY do by itself, without being wired to anything else?
options: Analyzes a table and recommends (and optionally applies) sensitivity tags — it does not mask data by itself
Automatically masks every column it identifies as sensitive
Deletes columns that contain sensitive data
Grants extra privileges to roles that need to see sensitive data
questions.explain: SYSTEM$CLASSIFY is a recommendation-and-tagging engine. It assigns system tags describing what a column is; masking only happens if a policy is separately wired to those tags, as in Lesson 10.

questions.q: What is the difference between a privacy category of IDENTIFIER and QUASI_IDENTIFIER?
options: IDENTIFIER directly identifies a person alone; QUASI_IDENTIFIER is only identifying in combination with other fields
IDENTIFIER applies only to numeric columns; QUASI_IDENTIFIER applies only to text columns
QUASI_IDENTIFIER is a stronger classification than IDENTIFIER
There is no practical difference — they are interchangeable labels
questions.explain: An email address is an IDENTIFIER because it identifies someone on its own. A birthdate is typically a QUASI_IDENTIFIER because it only becomes identifying combined with other fields, like city and gender.

questions.q: What changes when SYSTEM$CLASSIFY is called with {'auto_tag': true} compared to leaving auto_tag at its default?
options: The recommended tags are written to the table immediately, instead of only being recommended
auto_tag only controls whether a confidence score is shown
auto_tag: true disables the privacy_category output entirely
There is no difference — auto_tag has no effect on tagging
questions.explain: With auto_tag: false (the default if omitted), SYSTEM$CLASSIFY only recommends tags. With auto_tag: true, the recommended tags are written immediately.

questions.q: In the lesson's result for BIRTHDAY_DATE, what semantic_category was assigned?
options: DATE_OF_BIRTH
NAME
EMAIL
PHONE_NUMBER
questions.explain: The classification result for BIRTHDAY_DATE showed semantic_category: DATE_OF_BIRTH alongside privacy_category: QUASI_IDENTIFIER and confidence: HIGH.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe classification as 'the step before masking' rather than masking itself?
options: Classification only labels data with tags; those tags must separately be wired to a masking policy (as in Lesson 10) before anything is actually protected
Classification always runs after masking policies are already in place
Classification and masking are the same feature under two different names
Masking must be disabled before classification can run
questions.explain: Classification finds and labels sensitive columns with tags. Masking only happens when a policy is separately attached to those tags — the two features are composable, not the same thing.
